newsitem.title: USA: Perry to discuss future with Clinton this week.
newsitem.headline: Perry to discuss future with Clinton this week.

text.p: U.S. Defense Secretary William Perry said on Wednesday he would discuss his future with President Bill Clinton this week, but he refused to confirm reports that he had already told Clinton he plans to resign in the coming months.

"I have not submitted a letter of resignation. I have discussed several times with the President what my future plans are. I plan to meet with him later this week and discuss with him precisely what I would like to do and find out from him what he would like me to do," Perry said during a visit to U.S. Strategic Command headquarters here.

Earlier on Wednesday, a senior defense official said in Washington that Perry told his staff on Wednesday morning that he had told Clinton he wanted to leave, but was "flexible" and willing to wait until a successor was chosen.
"Until I have this discussion with him (Clinton), I am not prepared to make any announcement on that," Perry told reporters in response to questions. He declined to discuss the staff meeting.

But Perry also said that, during the past year or so, it had become increasingly difficult to deal with the Republican-led Congress on a bipartisan basis, apparently referring to legislative wrangling between Congress and the White House.

"There has been a much stronger partisan approach to defense issues. And this, I think has been a problem," said Perry, adding that he feared such bickering would continue in Clinton's second term. "It (partisanship) can very well decrease the ability of the United States to conduct a well-managed, well-organized defense program."
